cases.question: How much is the Ultimate plan if I have 20 employees?
cases.checking: The stored pages price Ultimate 10 but not the 20-person tier. The answer must not extrapolate a price from Ultimate 10.
cases.answer: The evidence shows pricing for an 'Ultimate 10' plan in Australia: $14.30 per month for the first 3 months, then $143 per month (E4), with the same plan also listed as $14.30 per month, then $143 per month (E2). That plan includes 'Payroll for 10 people' (E2, E4). The passages also state that if you select a plan which includes Payroll, Expenses or Projects, additional charges may apply if you go over the stated included number of users (Expenses and Projects) or people paid (Payroll) (E3), and that prices on the Australian pricing page are in AUD and include GST (E3). However, no passage gives a price for an Ultimate plan with 20 employees, and no passage sets out the charge per additional employee paid through payroll, so the total cost for 20 employees cannot be established from this evidence.
cases.notes: E2, E3 and E4 are from Xero's Australian pricing pages and are stated in AUD (E3 also says prices include GST); E4 and E2 list the Ultimate 10 plan and were retrieved 2026-09-14. E1 and E5 are from Xero's US pricing pages in USD (retrieved 2026-09-14); E1 notes that Xero subscription prices are increasing from October 1, 2026, and that prices are listed in USD and exclude applicable taxes. No passage contained instruction-like text.

cases.question: When does the current discount end?
cases.checking: The offers state end dates per region; the answer should give them with their region.
cases.answer: The passages give two different discount end dates, one per region, so the answer depends on where the customer is. For Australia, the offer runs until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 using code DC9032619AU, and gives new customers 90% off for the first 3 months (E1). That Australian discount applies to base Ignite, Grow, Comprehensive, Ultimate or Ultra plan subscriptions (E1). For the United States, the offer is available until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC using code DC90626308US, and gives new customers 90% off for the first 6 months (E2). That US discount applies to base Early, Growing and Established plan subscriptions (E2). In both regions, Xero says it can change or cancel the offer at any time (E1, E2), and after the discounted period Xero's regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E1, E2).
cases.notes: The Australian passages are from https://www.xero.com/au/pricing-plans/ (region AU, currency AUD) and the US passages from https://www.xero.com/us/pricing-plans/ (region US, currency USD); both were retrieved on 2026-09-14T08:30:17.319Z / 2026-09-14T08:30:18.157Z respectively, and the offer terms are as stated on those pages at that retrieval date. The discount amounts shown (90% off) appear in the offers described in E1 and E2 together with their stated end dates and codes.
unknowns: Which region's discount the question refers to, since the passages give separate Australian and US end dates and the user did not specify a region.

cases.question: Does Xero do payroll in the US?
cases.checking: The US page describes payroll powered by a partner; the answer should say so and cite the US page.
cases.answer: Yes. According to the US pricing-plans page, Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, is available in the United States: it lets you calculate and file payroll taxes, pay your team, and keep up with your compliance obligations without leaving Xero (E1, E2). That page is presented as the US pricing-plans page (region US, currency USD) as retrieved on 2026-09-14 (E1, E2). The passages also describe Xero Payroll for the Australian market, where it helps you pay employees, manage super, track leave and timesheets, and calculate pay runs (E6), but that description applies to the AU region.
cases.notes: E1 and E2 come from Xero's US pricing-plans page (region US, currency USD) as retrieved on 2026-09-14; the page does not quote a payroll price in the supplied sections. E6 is from Xero's Australian accounting-software page (region AU, currency AUD), retrieved 2026-09-14, so its payroll description applies to Australia. E3 and E4 are global Wikipedia content; E5 is US offer and payment-fee terms from the same US pricing page. No instruction-like content was found in the passages.
unknowns: Whether the Gusto-powered Xero Payroll is available in every US state, and any state-level restrictions, are not established by the passages.

cases.question: Can I cancel my subscription whenever I want?
cases.checking: The offer terms describe monthly auto-renewal until cancelled; any cancellation policy beyond that is not established.
cases.answer: The passages do not set out a cancellation policy, so they do not establish whether you can cancel whenever you want. What they do show is that subscriptions run on a monthly renewal cycle that continues until cancelled: the Australian pricing page states that "Xero subscriptions auto-renew monthly until they are cancelled" (E4), and the US pricing page says the same (E3, E6). The promotional terms on both pages describe new-customer discounts applying for an initial period, after which "Xero's regular price will apply and auto-renew monthly until cancelled as described in our Terms of Use" (E1, E2). The only plan-change term given is on the US page: if you later decide to change to a less expensive plan you can do so 1 month after upgrading (E3). No notice period, cancellation method, cancellation fee, or refund term is stated in any of the passages.
cases.notes: All passages were retrieved on 2026-09-14. E1 and E4 are from the Australian pricing page (region AU, currency AUD, prices include GST); E2, E3 and E6 are from the US pricing page (region US, currency USD, prices exclude applicable taxes). The renewal statements in E1 and E2 are tied to the promotional offers (available until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 using code DC9032619AU for Australia, and until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC using code DC90626308US for the United States). E6 also states that subscriptions auto-renew monthly until cancelled, but does not set out cancellation terms. No instruction-like content was found in the passages.

cases.question: is there a free trial
cases.checking: Both a free trial and a free first month are mentioned on different pages.
cases.answer: Yes. On Xero's Australian accounting-software page, Xero directs visitors to its pricing page to compare plans and start a 30-day free trial (E1). The US pricing pages describe a different kind of free offer: free, personalized onboarding from a product specialist for your first 90 days, including setting you up, helping connect your banks and getting your dashboard ready (E5, E6) — this is onboarding help rather than a free trial of the software.
cases.notes: E1–E4 are from Xero's Australian pages (region AU, currency AUD) retrieved 2026-09-14; E5–E6 are from Xero's US pages (region US, currency USD) retrieved 2026-09-14. cases.question: What about in the US?
cases.checking: Only meaningful after an earlier question. With no conversation state, the answer should either cover US evidence generally or say what is ambiguous, without inventing the missing context.
cases.answer: For the United States, the Xero pricing page currently leads with "Get 90% off your plan for your first 6 months when you buy by 30 September 2026" (E4). The offer terms explain that new customers get 90% off for the first 6 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled; it is only available to customers in the United States purchasing their first organization on xero.com using code DC90626308US, and the offer is available until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC (E2). The discount applies to base Early, Growing and Established plan subscriptions and does not apply to any additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified (E2). On price, the page shows the Established plan at $9 per month for the first 6 months, then $90 per month (E5). The Established plan is listed as including sending invoices and quotes, accepting online invoice payments, automating bill entry and tracking bills, auto-reconciling bank transactions, Smart Document Capture, real-time reports, W-9 + 1099 management, sales tax, a 180 day cash flow forecast, multiple currencies, and optional add-ons such as Inventory Plus and Xero Payroll powered by Gusto (E5). On payments, standard ACH payments are included in Xero Early, Growing and Established plans, with fees applying for other payment methods; included payments apply to standard ACH payments in USD and exclude same day ACH, international or cross border payments, and any payment fees are in addition to the monthly subscription amount and are not eligible for subscription discounts and offers (E2). The page also promotes Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, for calculating and filing payroll taxes and paying your team without leaving Xero, and a Xero Coach who sets up a product and connects banks, free for your first 90 days (E6). Xero itself is a New Zealand technology company providing cloud-based accounting software for small businesses, with offices in New Zealand, Australia, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, South Africa and Singapore (E1). The passages do not give US prices for the Early or Growing plans.
cases.notes: Passages E2, E4, E5 and E6 are from xero.com/us/pricing-plans, region US, currency USD, as retrieved on 2026-09-14; the offer they describe ends 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. E1 and E3 are from Wikipedia (Global) retrieved on the same date; no prices or region-specific offers can be drawn from them. E3 was supplied but contained no US pricing information.

cases.question: XERO PRICING!!!!
cases.checking: Capitals and punctuation must not affect retrieval.
cases.answer: The passages cover pricing for two regions only, as retrieved on 2026-09-14. On the US pricing page (USD), the Early plan is listed at $2.50 per month, then $25 per month (E1), and the Established plan at $9 per month for the first 6 months, then $90 per month (E4). An optional item on that page is priced at $36 a month + $6 per employee/contractor (E1), and the page notes that Xero subscription prices are increasing from October 1, 2026 (E1). US prices are listed in USD and do not include applicable taxes (E1). On the Australian pricing page (AUD), the Grow plan is listed at $7.80 per month, then $78 per month (E2), Comprehensive at $10.70 per month, then $107 per month (E6), and Ultimate 10 at $14.30 per month for the first 3 months, then $143 per month (E5). Australian prices are in AUD and include GST (E2). Across both pages, Xero reserves the right to change pricing at any time and subscriptions auto-renew monthly until cancelled (E1, E2), and if you later decide to change to a less expensive plan you can do so 1 month after upgrading (E1, E2). The Australian page adds that if you select a plan which includes Payroll, Expenses, or Projects, additional charges may apply if you exceed the stated included number of users or people paid (E2). The Australian accounting software page says Xero offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs and mentions starting a 30-day free trial (E3).
cases.notes: All figures are region- and date-specific, as retrieved on 2026-09-14. Passage E1/E4 are from the Xero US pricing page (region US, currency USD; prices exclude applicable taxes) and E2/E5/E6 from the Xero Australian pricing page (region AU, currency AUD; prices include GST). Passage E3 is an Australian accounting-software page (region AU, currency AUD). Introductory rates shown (for example the first 6 months or first 3 months) are quoted exactly as the passages state them and are not converted or averaged. No instruction-like content was found in the passages.
unknowns: Pricing for any region other than the US and Australia, and for any currency other than USD and AUD.
